content.caseIdentity: Abdul Rehman Antulay v. R.S. Nayak, (1992) 1 SCC 225; AIR 1992 SC 1701
content.facts: A Constitution Bench considered the Article 21 right to speedy trial and the effect of prolonged delay in criminal proceedings.
questionsBeforeCourt: Whether speedy trial is part of Article 21.
How delay should be assessed and what remedies may follow.
Whether a rigid universal time-limit should terminate every delayed prosecution.
content.ratioDecidendi: The right to speedy trial is an integral part of Article 21. Delay must be assessed contextually, considering responsibility for delay, nature of offence, witnesses, court workload, systemic conditions and prejudice; no rigid universal outer limit applies to every prosecution.
content.holding: The Court rejected a fixed automatic time-bar for every delayed prosecution and laid down contextual principles for assessing Article 21 violations and remedies.
content.relevance: Leading Constitution Bench authority on speedy trial under Article 21.

sources.label: Official Supreme Court judgment expressly citing A.R. Antulay, (1992) 1 SCC 225 and its speedy-trial proposition.
